claim_text: The conventional VH-VL interface is a reproducible empirical structural surface rather than only the classical FR2 tetrad.
source_variable_or_result: 28-position primary_binary_interface set (delta-SASA-derived, translated-far-away control confirmed genuine occlusion)
effect_size_or_summary: 28 positions, spanning FR2/FR3/CDR3/FR4, not limited to IMGT 42/49/50/52
robustness_status: validated on real-structure sample + translated-far-away geometric control (Stage 3)
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED: the empirical former VH-VL interface spans 28 IMGT positions, of which only 4 are the classical tetrad
prohibited_overclaim: Do not say the interface IS the tetrad, or that the tetrad alone explains VL loss accommodation

claim_text: VHHs show distinct amino-acid chemistry at the former-interface relative to conventional VH.
effect_direction: VHH lower (less hydrophobic, more charged-favoring) than VH
stage11_adjusted_status: Formally tested, Family A hypothesis A
robustness_status: BH-FDR q=4.4e-86, PDB-cluster p=2.9e-87, permutation p=0.0002 -- STABLE
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED + statistically ASSOCIATED: VHH former-interface intrinsic sequence chemistry differs from conventional VH (standardized effect -0.91)
prohibited_overclaim: Do not claim this alone explains solubility

claim_text: The sequence-level chemical adaptation is reflected in the native solvent-exposed 3D surface.
effect_direction: VHH lower native surface hydrophobicity than VH; H_intrinsic strongly predicts native surface (R2=0.52)
stage11_adjusted_status: Group: Family A hypothesis B (q=1.8e-253). Mechanism: ModelC1 R2=0.522, p=2.2e-128
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED + ASSOCIATED: native exposed former-interface chemistry differs VHH-vs-VH and is strongly predicted by intrinsic sequence chemistry
prohibited_overclaim: Do not claim sequence chemistry fully explains native surface (R2=0.52, not 1.0; shielding adds independent information, see Claim L)

claim_text: CDR3 physically shields a substantial portion of the non-CDR3 former-interface in native VHH structures.
effect_direction: positive shielding observed in all 533 VHH structures
stage11_adjusted_status: not a group-comparison hypothesis (VHH-only geometric counterfactual)
robustness_status: validated via same-coordinate no-CDR3 SASA counterfactual, translated-far-away control (Stage 6)
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED: CDR3 removal (geometric SASA counterfactual) increases exposure at the 15-position shieldable former interface in all 533 VHH structures
prohibited_overclaim: Do not call the no-CDR3 state a physical mutant or claim CDR3 "replaces" VL

claim_text: CDR3 shielding is geometrically coupled to CDR3-former-interface packing.
stage11_adjusted_status: Formally quantified as inseparable (Stage 11 collinearity gate)
robustness_status: confirmed severe, not estimable as independent predictors
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED + HIGHLY COUPLED: shielding and CDR3-target packing (BSA) are so strongly correlated that their independent contributions cannot be reliably separated in this dataset
prohibited_overclaim: Never present shielding and BSA as two independent parallel mechanisms or interpret a coefficient difference between them as evidence of distinct mechanisms

claim_text: VHH former-interface hydrophobic surface organization differs from VH, including lower PSH / smaller hydrophobic patch organization.
effect_direction: VHH lower PSH and smaller largest patch than VH
stage11_adjusted_status: Family A hypotheses C (PSH q=1.4e-11; largest patch q=5.8e-55)
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED + statistically ASSOCIATED: VHH shows lower former-interface PSH and smaller largest hydrophobic patch than conventional VH
prohibited_overclaim: Do not equate PSH/patch-size difference with lower aggregation propensity (not tested)

claim_text: VHH former-interface electrostatics differ from VH, but cannot be summarized as a simple positive-vs-negative shift.
effect_direction: VHH more positive in positive component (118.3 vs 115.4) AND more negative in negative component (-168.2 vs -157.3)
robustness_status: corrected in Stage-8 closure audit; re-verified in Stage 9/11 as separate components throughout
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED: VHH shows stronger potential magnitude in BOTH the positive and negative components sampled at exposed former-interface atoms, not a uniform directional shift
prohibited_overclaim: Never write "VHH is more electropositive" or "less negative"; never construct positive-minus-negative net score; never call this a solvent-excluded molecular-surface integral

claim_text: VHH antigen-interface organization differs from conventional antibody organization, including greater framework participation.
source_variable_or_result: framework_contact_fraction, cdr3_contact_fraction, VHH vs conventional VH
effect_direction: VHH higher framework fraction (0.209 vs 0.163) and higher CDR3 fraction (0.470 vs 0.403) than VH
stage11_adjusted_status: Family A hypotheses D (q=9.3e-8) and F (q=1.2e-12)
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED + statistically ASSOCIATED: VHH shows significantly greater framework participation and CDR3 dominance in antigen contacts than conventional VH
prohibited_overclaim: Do not equate framework participation with higher affinity or "better" binding; do not reduce to FR2 alone (FR1/FR3/FR4 all contribute, Stage 9)

claim_text: The former VH-VL surface remains antigen-accessible in a subset of VHHs rather than becoming universally functionally occluded.
source_variable_or_result: shieldable_engagement_fraction (mean 0.186, N=533; 33.6% structures show zero engagement, but 66.4% show nonzero)
effect_size_or_summary: mean 18.6% of 15-position interface contacts antigen; two-part sensitivity confirms both presence and magnitude vary
stage11_adjusted_status: descriptive distributional fact, not a formal hypothesis test
robustness_status: confirmed via manual validation (Stage 9), both high- and zero-engagement VHH cases genuinely exist
allowed_final_wording: OBSERVED: the former VH-VL surface participates in antigen engagement in a majority but not all VHH structures (66.4% nonzero at the 15-position level)
prohibited_overclaim: Do not say every former-interface residue remains functional, and do not say the interface is universally sealed

claim_text: The descriptive shielding-antigen-engagement relationship does NOT represent a robust independent shielding effect after CDR3 geometry adjustment.
effect_size_or_summary: Model4C std-beta=-0.146 p=0.065 (q=0.077); Model5B std-beta=0.082 p=0.196 (q=0.212); Model6B std-beta=-0.083 p=0.243 (q=0.243) -- all three formally nonsignificant after adjusting for CDR3 length (+FR2_CDR3_Dis)
stage11_adjusted_status: Formally tested and null in the fully-adjusted models (VIF<4, not a numerical-instability artifact)
robustness_status: attenuation itself confirmed MOSTLY_STABLE across sensitivities (Stage 11 Section R)
allowed_final_wording: ASSOCIATED (unadjusted) but NOT_SUPPORTED as an independent effect after adjustment: the raw shielding-vs-engagement relationship is robust and significant, but does not survive CDR3-geometry adjustment
prohibited_overclaim: Never draw shielding -> reduced antigen engagement as a standalone causal or strong independent arrow
notes: This is the single most important correction carried into the final mechanism figure

claim_text: CDR3 geometry is a shared organizing variable connecting shielding and antigen-interface redistribution.
source_variable_or_result: cdr3_sequence_length as dominant predictor in Model4B/4C, Model5B, Model6B
effect_direction: CDR3 length remains significant (p<1e-10) in every adjusted model where shielding becomes null
stage11_adjusted_status: Formally supported: CDR3 length independently significant in Model1A (shielding), Model4B/4C (engagement), Model5B (CDR3 fraction), Model6B (framework fraction)
robustness_status: STABLE (influence-exclusion, resolution-adjustment, high-coverage all preserve significance)
allowed_final_wording: ASSOCIATED: CDR3 length (and related geometry descriptors) independently associates with both shielding and antigen-interface organization measures, consistent with a shared underlying geometric axis
prohibited_overclaim: Do not say "CDR3 length causes the VHH phenotype" -- this is a statistical association across nested models, not a causal demonstration

claim_text: Sequence chemistry and shielding both retain independent association with native/surface patch phenotype where supported by Stage 11.
source_variable_or_result: ModelC2: H_intrinsic + shielding -> native_surface (both significant); ModelD2: H_intrinsic + native_surface + shielding -> PSH (all three significant)
effect_direction: all positive/negative as expected, all independently significant
effect_size_or_summary: ModelC2 R2=0.578 (vs 0.522 H_intrinsic alone); ModelD2 R2=0.230 (vs 0.115 H_intrinsic alone), VIF<2.5 throughout
stage11_adjusted_status: Formally tested and supported, well-conditioned (not a collinearity artifact)
allowed_final_wording: ASSOCIATED: shielding contributes independent information about native surface chemistry and PSH phenotype beyond intrinsic sequence chemistry alone
prohibited_overclaim: Do not imply shielding replaces sequence-level adaptation, or vice versa -- both are complementary, independently-supported forms of accommodation
